subject: English
q: Pakistan’s industrial sector grew rapidly in ______ 1960s.
explanation: Decades take ‘the’ (the 1960s).

subject: English
q: By coincidence the two sisters wore ______ same dress to the wedding.
explanation: ‘Same’ is always preceded by ‘the’.

subject: English
q: We usually go for a walk in ______ evening.
explanation: Parts of the day after ‘in’ take ‘the’ (in the morning, in the evening).

subject: English
q: ______ Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal.
explanation: A descriptive title placed before a name takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Allama Iqbal is often called ______ Poet of the East.
explanation: A unique epithet or title takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Government of Pakistan has announced a relief package for flood victims.
explanation: Official bodies named with ‘of’ take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Lahore of the Mughal era was a great centre of art and learning.
explanation: A proper noun that is restricted by a qualifying phrase (of the Mughal era) takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: A doctor must earn ______ trust of his patients.
explanation: An abstract noun followed by an ‘of’ phrase that makes it specific takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Kashmir dispute remains the core issue between Pakistan and India.
explanation: When a proper name is used as a modifier before a common noun (the Kashmir dispute), the noun takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: The British Crown took direct control of India after ______ War of Independence of 1857.
explanation: Names of particular historic wars and events take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Every monsoon ______ Indus floods low-lying parts of Sindh.
explanation: Names of rivers take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Climbers from many countries visit ______ Himalayas every year.
explanation: Names of mountain ranges take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ United Nations was founded in 1945.
explanation: Names of organisations with ‘United’ or plural forms take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China.
explanation: Names of highways and famous roads of this kind take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Thar Desert extends across Pakistan and India.
explanation: Names of deserts take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Pacific is the largest ocean on Earth.
explanation: Names of oceans and seas take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Netherlands is famous for its tulips and windmills.
explanation: Country names that are plural in form take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: What ______ lovely garden you have!
explanation: In exclamations with ‘what’ and a singular countable noun, ‘a/an’ is used.

subject: English
q: He earns sixty thousand rupees ______ month.
explanation: ‘A/an’ is used to mean ‘per’ in expressions of rate.

subject: English
q: I have never heard such ______ absurd excuse.
explanation: ‘Such’ is followed by ‘a/an’ before a singular countable noun; ‘absurd’ begins with a vowel sound.

subject: English
q: It was quite ______ difficult paper, but most candidates finished it.
explanation: With ‘quite’, the article follows it: quite a difficult paper.

subject: English
q: Many ______ student has failed this paper through careless reading.
explanation: ‘Many a’ is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.

subject: English
q: As ______ result of the strike, all flights were cancelled.
explanation: The fixed phrase is ‘as a result of’.

subject: English
q: He left in ______ hurry and forgot his phone.
explanation: The fixed phrase is ‘in a hurry’.

subject: English
q: I am at ______ loss to explain his behaviour.
explanation: The fixed phrase is ‘at a loss’, meaning ‘unable to understand or decide’.

subject: English
q: On ______ whole, the budget was well received.
explanation: The fixed phrase is ‘on the whole’, meaning ‘in general’.

subject: English
q: ______ little knowledge is a dangerous thing.
explanation: The proverb uses ‘a little’, meaning ‘some, a small amount of’.

subject: English
q: My uncle is ______ lawyer in the Sindh High Court.
explanation: A singular countable noun naming someone’s profession takes ‘a/an’.

subject: English
q: ______ more you practise, ______ better you become.
explanation: The ‘the … the’ construction with comparatives shows two things changing together.

subject: English
q: Can you give me ______ advice on choosing a career?
explanation: ‘Advice’ is uncountable, so it cannot take ‘a/an’ or ‘many’; ‘some’ is used.

subject: English
q: The patient is so weak that there is ______ hope of his recovery.
explanation: ‘Little’ without an article means ‘hardly any’, which fits the negative sense; ‘few’ is for countable nouns.

subject: English
q: ______ few friends he had all deserted him in his hour of need.
explanation: ‘The few’ means ‘the small number that exist(ed)’, i.e. all of them.

subject: English
q: I still have ______ few friends in Lahore, so I never feel lonely there.
explanation: ‘A few’ means ‘some’, which suits the positive sense of the sentence.

subject: English
q: Could you pass me ______ salt, please?
explanation: Something both speakers can identify (the salt on the table) takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: There are two roads to the village; you can take ______ road.
explanation: ‘Either’ refers to one of two; ‘any’ and ‘every’ are used for more than two.

subject: English
q: The examiner gave ______ candidate a separate question paper.
explanation: ‘Each’ takes a singular noun and treats members individually; ‘all’, ‘both’ and ‘many’ need plural nouns.

subject: English
q: We do not have ______ time left before the deadline.
explanation: ‘Much’ is used with uncountable nouns such as ‘time’; the others go with countable nouns.

subject: English
q: This year ______ candidates passed the written examination than last year.
explanation: ‘Fewer’ is used with plural countable nouns; ‘less’ is for uncountable nouns.

subject: English
q: I bought a pen and a notebook yesterday, but I have already lost ______ pen.
explanation: A noun mentioned for the second time is now definite and takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: I ______ him since we left school.
explanation: An action continuing from a past point up to now, marked by ‘since’, takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: She ______ in Lahore for ten years and still lives there.
explanation: A situation that began in the past and continues now (‘still lives there’) takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: The deputy commissioner ______ his report to the ministry yesterday.
explanation: A finished past time such as ‘yesterday’ requires the simple past, not the present perfect.

subject: English
q: Don’t disturb her; she ______ just ______ asleep.
explanation: ‘Just’ describing a very recent action with a present result takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: ______ you ever ______ to Gilgit-Baltistan?
explanation: Questions about life experience up to now with ‘ever’ use the present perfect.

subject: English
q: You needn’t remind me; I ______ my homework already.
explanation: ‘Already’ with a result relevant now takes the present perfect in British usage.

subject: English
q: The results ______ yet, so we will have to wait.
explanation: ‘Not … yet’ with a present consequence takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: He ______ his keys, so he cannot open the door.
explanation: A past action whose result is felt now (he cannot open the door) takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: The young novelist ______ three books so far.
explanation: ‘So far’ indicates a period up to now and takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: Shakespeare ______ thirty-seven plays.
explanation: Actions of a person who is no longer living belong to a finished period and take the simple past.

subject: English
q: My grandfather ______ in the army for thirty years before he retired in 1990.
explanation: A completed period in the past (ended in 1990) takes the simple past.

subject: English
q: Pakistan ______ its first constitution in 1956.
explanation: A past event at a stated past time takes the simple past.

subject: English
q: Last night I ______ a strange dream.
explanation: ‘Last night’ is a finished time, so the simple past is used.

subject: English
q: The price of petrol ______ three times so far this year.
explanation: ‘This year’ is an unfinished period, so a series of changes within it takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: This is the first time I ______ in an aeroplane.
explanation: After ‘This is the first time’, the present perfect is used.

subject: English
q: It is the third time this week that he ______ late for the meeting.
explanation: After ‘It is the second/third time’, the present perfect is required.

subject: English
q: I ______ the novel you lent me; here it is.
explanation: A recently completed action with a present result (returning the book now) takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: Two years ______ since he left for Canada.
explanation: A period measured from a past point up to now (since he left) takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: She ______ ill since last Monday.
explanation: A state lasting from a past point until now, marked by ‘since’, takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: Since 2010 the city ______ rapidly towards the motorway.
explanation: Change over a period from a past point up to the present takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: I ______ for you since morning; where have you been?
explanation: An activity that started in the past and is still going on now takes the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: I ______ this book for a week; I am on the last chapter now.
explanation: An ongoing activity over a period up to now, with ‘for’, takes the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: He looks exhausted because he ______ in the fields since dawn.
explanation: The present perfect continuous explains present evidence (he looks exhausted) of a recent ongoing activity.

subject: English
q: Why are your eyes red? ______ you ______?
explanation: Present evidence of a recent continuous activity is explained with the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: The baby ______ for an hour; I wish it would stop.
explanation: An activity that has lasted for a period and is still continuing takes the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: The doctors ______ on strike for a week now.
explanation: ‘For a week now’ describes a situation continuing up to the present, which takes the present perfect.

subject: English
q: When we reached the station, the train ______.
explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

subject: English
q: By the time the police arrived, the thieves ______.
explanation: ‘By the time’ plus a past event shows that another action was completed before it, requiring the past perfect.

subject: English
q: The patient ______ before the doctor came.
explanation: An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect.

subject: English
q: He ______ snow until he visited Naran last winter.
explanation: Experience up to a point in the past (until he visited) takes the past perfect.

subject: English
q: When I got home, I found that someone ______ into the house.
explanation: An action that happened before the moment of discovery in the past takes the past perfect.

subject: English
q: She was nervous because she ______ in public before.
explanation: Experience before a past moment is expressed with the past perfect.

subject: English
q: They ______ each other for years before they got married.
explanation: A state lasting up to a past event takes the past perfect; ‘know’ is not used in the continuous.

subject: English
q: The children ______ asleep by the time we got home.
explanation: ‘By the time’ with a past event requires the past perfect for the earlier completed action.

subject: English
q: She was tired because she ______ all day without a break.
explanation: An activity continuing up to a past moment and explaining it takes the past perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: He ______ for two hours when the power failed.
explanation: The duration of an activity up to a past event is expressed by the past perfect continuous.

subject: English
q: He turned pale and looked as though he ______ a ghost.
explanation: After ‘as though’ referring to an unreal earlier event in the past, the past perfect is used.

subject: English
q: Look! The children ______ in the rain.
explanation: An action happening at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous.

subject: English
q: Listen! Someone ______ at the door.
explanation: ‘Listen!’ draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used.

subject: English
q: He ______ his driving test next Tuesday, so he is practising every day.
explanation: The present continuous can express a fixed personal arrangement in the future.

subject: English
q: She ______ her keys — she is so careless!
explanation: The present continuous with ‘always’ expresses a repeated action that annoys the speaker.
